newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea unions threaten poll defeat for ruling party.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea unions threaten poll defeat for ruling party.

text.p: South Korea's two major union bodies on Tuesday threatened to continue struggling for worker rights until presidential elections in December and said they would combine forces to defeat the ruling party's candidate.

In their first ever formal meeting, the heads of the officially-sanctioned Federation of Korean Trade Unions and the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions said they would carry out the threat if the government did not revoke a controversial labour law.

"Unless the law is revised...our struggle will continue until the presidential elections and there will be a judgement on the New Korea Party's candidate," confederation president Kwon Young-kil told reporters.
In a joint statement, Kwon and federation president Park In-sang said the two unions would for the first time organise a joint rally against the government. No other details were given.
Park did not comment on the poor turnout of the federation's two-day nationwide strike that began on Tuesday.
The two unions -- normally arch rivals -- urged their members to follow a call for all-out strikes on Wednesday.
